identification.name: AISI 4130 Steel (Normalized)
identification.common_form_notes: Widely stocked as seamless tube ("4130 chromoly") for aircraft engine mounts, roll cages, and tube-frame chassis, as well as round bar, sheet, and plate. The normalized condition shown here is a lower-strength baseline/as-received state; quenched-and-tempered variants (see MatWeb's water-quenched + temper conditions) are more commonly specified where higher strength is needed.
identification.notes: Normalized condition (870°C/1600°F austenitized, air cooled) — chosen specifically to match the material tested in NACA TN 2324 and NASA TN D-111 (Grover, Bishop, Hyler, and Jackson; Battelle Memorial Institute, 1951/1959), used elsewhere in this database for aluminum fatigue-strength comparisons. This is NOT the quenched-and-tempered condition most commonly specified for chromoly tubing/roll-cage applications (which reaches substantially higher strength at some cost to ductility). Values were cross-checked between MatWeb's two "normalized" page variants (no size specified vs. 25 mm/1 in round); only reduction of area differed marginally (60% vs 59.5%), so this entry uses the no-size-specified page as primary. Shear strength (387 MPa) derived via von Mises criterion (UTS (ultimate tensile strength)/√3) since no directly-reported value was available and this condition is ductile (25.5% elongation). Electrical conductivity (7.7% IACS (International Annealed Copper Standard)) derived from the source's stated electrical resistivity (22.3 µΩ·cm at 20°C) via %IACS = (1.7241/22.3)×100; the source annotates that resistivity figure as measured on a "hardened and tempered" specimen even on this normalized-condition page, suggesting MatWeb reuses one generic resistivity table across several 4130 heat-treatment pages rather than measuring it per-condition — treat this figure as approximate. Specific heat and thermal conductivity are MatWeb's banded generic-4130 figures, not precise single-temperature measurements: specific heat is reported for the >=100°C, 150–200°C, and 750–800°C bands (stored here at 100/175/775°C); thermal conductivity is reported at 100°C, 300°C, and 1200°C. Hardness values other than Brinell (Vickers, Rockwell B/C, Knoop) are MatWeb-converted from the directly-measured Brinell value, not independently measured. No melting point, fracture toughness, coefficient of thermal expansion, or fatigue data was available from these source pages.

typical_usage: Aircraft engine mounts and landing gear components, roll cages and tube-frame chassis in motorsport, high-pressure gas cylinders, gears, and machine parts requiring good weldability combined with moderate strength. The normalized condition serves as a common baseline/as-received state; quenched-and-tempered variants are used where higher strength is required.
